extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: DocVQA is a large scale dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images. The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Questions are categorized based on reasoning requirements (9 question types: handwritten, form, layout, table/list, running text, photograph, figure, yes/no, other). The dataset is split 80/10/10 into train (39,463 questions, 10,194 images), validation (5,349 questions, 1,286 images), and test (5,188 questions, 1,287 images) sets.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.publisher: CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, India and Computer Vision Center, UAB, Spain
extraction.citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3 [cs.CV], 5 Jan 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Documents were downloaded from different collections and pages were hand-picked for use in the dataset. Binarized images were minimized to avoid poor image quality as a bottleneck. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. Questions and answers were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage annotation process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library (https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/), organized under different industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical) and collections. The final set of images is drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents spanning from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from 1900 to 2018, with most documents from the 1960-2000 period.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: OCR tokens from document images were serialized to a single string separated by space in top-left to bottom-right order. For BERT QA models, answer spans were approximated by finding the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string, following an approach proposed in TriviaQA.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Binarized images were minimized in the dataset. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized. Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity during stage 2 annotation were excluded from the dataset. Questions where none of the answers from stage 1 matched any answers from stage 2 were sent for a third-stage review, where they were either accepted (after editing if necessary) or ignored. OCR tokens were extracted using a commercial OCR application for use in experiments.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages. Stage 1: Remote workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs. Workers were encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer per question where warranted, and instructed to ask questions answerable using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. Stage 2: A different worker was shown the image and questions from stage 1 (without stage 1 answers) and required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag questions as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity. Stage 3: If none of the answers from stage 1 matched any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review by the authors, who could edit questions and answers before accepting or ignoring them.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Web-based annotation tool (custom, screen grabs shown in appendix)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: If none of the answers entered in stage 1 match exactly with any answers from stage 2, the question is sent for third-stage review by the authors. Questions flagged as inapt in stage 2 are not included in the dataset. The annotation process ensures multiple ground truth answers per question where warranted.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image; multiple ground truth answers per question where warranted; each question annotated by at least 2 workers (stage 1 and stage 2)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR application (used for extracting OCR tokens from document images in experiments)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org. No explicit versioning, update timeframe, or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains document images from industry documents that may include names of people, institutions, and places as answers. Named entities such as names of people appear among the most frequent non-numeric answers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: DocVQA aims to inspire a 'purpose-driven' approach in Document Analysis and Recognition (DAR) research, enabling intelligent reading systems to respond to ad-hoc information requests expressed in natural language. This could drive methods that use low-level cues (text, layout, arrangements) and high-level goals (purpose, relationship, domain knowledge) in solving problems of practical importance.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: A large majority of questions start with 'what is the', asking for date, title, total, amount or name. There are questions repeatedly asked about dates, titles and page numbers. Almost all top answers are numeric values, reflecting the prevalence of reports and invoices. Many documents are from food and nutrition related collections due to availability of non-binarized images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the UCSF library are binarized, which takes a toll on image quality; binarized images were minimized but not entirely excluded. OCR errors can result in wrong answers even when models correctly ground questions. Models struggle with questions requiring understanding of document structure, figures, diagrams, and handwritten text. The dataset is limited to documents from 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical) from the UCSF Industry Documents Library.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing of Visual Question Answering (VQA) models on document images. The dataset is intended to drive 'purpose-driven' document image analysis and recognition research. It can be used to evaluate reading comprehension models and scene text VQA models on document images. A leaderboard is available at docvqa.org for benchmarking.
